content.text:
**Medi-Cal** is California’s Medicaid program. It offers **free or low-cost health coverage** for eligible California residents, including many low-income adults, children, pregnant people, seniors, and people with disabilities. California says Medi-Cal coverage is available to eligible Californians **regardless of immigration status**. ([ca.gov](https://www.ca.gov/departments/217/services/37/?utm_source=openai))

You can apply for Medi-Cal:

- **Online** through Covered California or BenefitsCal
- **By phone**
- **By mail**
- **In person** at your county social services office ([dhcs.ca.gov](https://www.dhcs.ca.gov/medi-cal/apply/?utm_source=openai))

To check if you qualify, Medi-Cal eligibility is generally based on things like **household size, income, age, disability status, pregnancy, and other circumstances**. DHCS has an official “Qualify” page and eligibility charts. ([dhcs.ca.gov](https://www.dhcs.ca.gov/medi-cal/qualify/?utm_source=openai))

If you tell me what you need—**apply, renew, check eligibility, find a doctor, replace a card, or understand benefits**—I can help you with the next steps.
